title: collectReward with zero totalStaked is silently lossy: rewardPerSecond is set immediately, but _updatePool early-returns when totalStaked==0, allowing the depletion clock to consume funded rewards before any staker can claim
rootCause: `_updatePool` early-returns when `totalStaked == 0` advancing `lastRewardTime` without depleting `rewardBalance`. `collectReward` unconditionally re-anchors `rewardPerSecond` against the full depletionDuration regardless of staker presence. Net: funders deposit at zero-TVL pay for a depletion window that the clock skips; new entrants get either a windfall or a shortened effective window, depending on timing.
impactSummary: Funder-side: deposits made during zero-staked periods silently park value that won't be distributed in the advertised window. Staker-side: entrants after a zero-staked gap may capture orphan rewardBalance.
preservedDetails: ECON-008 carries the full analysis (timeline walkthrough, drained-then-empty variant, profile §5 'benign locally' challenge).
remediation: Either revert collectReward when totalStaked==0, or pause the depletion clock during zero-TVL periods, or compute rewardPerSecond against remainingDepletionTime instead of full depletionDuration.
dedupNotes: Distinct from DEDUP-001 (V1 re-anchor) — that bug is the per-interaction asymptotic decay; this is the OPPOSITE problem (silent value parked when no staker is present). Both follow from the rate formula being decoupled from elapsed-time accounting, but they manifest in opposite directions.
